raw: {"mode":"iff","restated":"∃ (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (Tstar : ℝ) (v : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ HasCompactSupport u₀ ∧ u₀ ≠ 0 ∧ Tstar ∈ Set.Ioc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Ico 0 Tstar) u₀ v p ∧ (∃ E : ℝ, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) Tstar, (∫ x : ℝ³, ‖v x t‖ ^ 2) < E) ∧ (∀ T : ℝ, 0 < T → ((∃ w q, EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Icc 0 T) u₀ w q) ↔ T < Tstar)) ∧ (∀ T ∈ Ioo 0 Tstar, (⨆ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) T, velocityC1Norm (v · t)) < ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ t in Ico (0 : ℝ) T, vorticityNorm (v · t)) < ⊤) ∧ Filter.limsup (fun t : ℝ => velocityC1Norm (v · t)) (𝓝[<] Tstar) = ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ t in Ico (0 : ℝ) Tstar, vorticityNorm (v · t)) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (w : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (q : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), ¬ EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3 u₀ w q","proof":"simp only [not_exists, Set.mem_Ioc]","english":"There is nonzero, compactly supported, rapidly decaying smooth divergence-free initial data u₀ and a maximal time Tstar in (0,1] with a Sobolev-class Euler solution on [0,Tstar), with bounded energy, such that closed-interval solutions exist exactly for T < Tstar, C¹ norm and vorticity integral are finite on shorter intervals, the C¹ norm has infinite limsup at Tstar, the vorticity integral over [0,Tstar) is infinite, and for every pair (w,q) the pair fails to be a global smooth finite-energy Euler solution.","why_clearer":"It writes the time bound as Tstar ∈ (0,1] and turns the final nonexistence clause into an explicit 'for all (w,q), not a global solution' statement."}

parsed.restated: ∃ (u₀ : ℝ³ → ℝ³) (Tstar : ℝ) (v : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (p : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), InitialVelocityConditionDecay u₀ ∧ HasCompactSupport u₀ ∧ u₀ ≠ 0 ∧ Tstar ∈ Set.Ioc (0:ℝ) 1 ∧ EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Ico 0 Tstar) u₀ v p ∧ (∃ E : ℝ, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) Tstar, (∫ x : ℝ³, ‖v x t‖ ^ 2) < E) ∧ (∀ T : ℝ, 0 < T → ((∃ w q, EulerSobolevExistenceAndSmoothnessR3On (Icc 0 T) u₀ w q) ↔ T < Tstar)) ∧ (∀ T ∈ Ioo 0 Tstar, (⨆ t ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) T, velocityC1Norm (v · t)) < ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ t in Ico (0 : ℝ) T, vorticityNorm (v · t)) < ⊤) ∧ Filter.limsup (fun t : ℝ => velocityC1Norm (v · t)) (𝓝[<] Tstar) = ⊤ ∧ (∫⁻ t in Ico (0 : ℝ) Tstar, vorticityNorm (v · t)) = ⊤ ∧ ∀ (w : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ³) (q : ℝ³ → ℝ → ℝ), ¬ EulerExistenceAndSmoothnessR3 u₀ w q
parsed.english: There is nonzero, compactly supported, rapidly decaying smooth divergence-free initial data u₀ and a maximal time Tstar in (0,1] with a Sobolev-class Euler solution on [0,Tstar), with bounded energy, such that closed-interval solutions exist exactly for T < Tstar, C¹ norm and vorticity integral are finite on shorter intervals, the C¹ norm has infinite limsup at Tstar, the vorticity integral over [0,Tstar) is infinite, and for every pair (w,q) the pair fails to be a global smooth finite-energy Euler solution.
parsed.why_clearer: It writes the time bound as Tstar ∈ (0,1] and turns the final nonexistence clause into an explicit 'for all (w,q), not a global solution' statement.
